source: ប្រភេទស្មៅដែលដុះក្នុងស្រែ (Types of Weeds Growing in Rice Fields), agrochemical product-training slide deck for the Hai Au Agro brand herbicides 'Hai Au YOYO 300EC' (Pretilachlor 300g/L + Fenclorim 100g/L) and 'Hai Au Alo 200EC' (Cyhalofop-butyl 200g/L); no institutional letterhead, presenter name, or date visible anywhere in the deck
text:
Hai Au Alo 200EC contains Cyhalofop-butyl 200 g/L and is a post-emergent, grass-selective herbicide used against grass weeds already growing in the rice field, without harming the rice plant itself. It is absorbed through the weed's leaves and translocated to the roots, stopping growth of the actively growing grass weed.

Timing and rate: for broadcast rice, apply 7-15 days after sowing at 20 ml per 16-liter backpack sprayer (2 backpacks per 1,000 m²); for transplanted rice, apply 15-30 days after transplanting at a higher rate of 40 ml per 16-liter backpack sprayer. The source shows the herbicide's effect on treated grass weeds (browning and dying back) within about 5-7 days after spraying, comparing plots before and after treatment, and notes that rice tillering recovers and fills in the treated area within about 1-2 days of water re-entering the plot after application, with clearly visible crop recovery within 4-5 days.
